cases.summary: Postpartum thyroiditis followed across its thyrotoxic, hypothyroid and recovery phases. The case is built so that a clinician who sees only the first phase will reach for a thionamide, and one who sees only the second will start lifelong levothyroxine - both wrong.

summary_i18n.en: Postpartum thyroiditis across thyrotoxic, hypothyroid and recovery phases; each phase in isolation invites the wrong treatment.
summary_i18n.de: Postpartum-Thyreoiditis über thyreotoxische, hypothyreote und Erholungsphase; jede Phase für sich verleitet zur falschen Therapie.
summary_i18n.es: Tiroiditis posparto a lo largo de sus fases tirotóxica, hipotiroidea y de recuperación; cada fase aislada induce al tratamiento equivocado.
summary_i18n.nl: Postpartum thyreoïditis door thyreotoxische, hypothyreote en herstelfase; elke fase apart lokt de verkeerde behandeling uit.
summary_i18n.ru: Послеродовой тиреоидит в тиреотоксической, гипотиреоидной и восстановительной фазах; каждая фаза по отдельности провоцирует неверное лечение.

cases.author: MedSimQA Editorial

presentation.chief_complaint: Palpitations, irritability and difficulty sleeping ten weeks after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery.

chief_complaint_i18n.en: Palpitations, irritability and insomnia ten weeks after an uncomplicated delivery.
chief_complaint_i18n.de: Palpitationen, Reizbarkeit und Schlaflosigkeit zehn Wochen nach unkomplizierter Entbindung.
chief_complaint_i18n.es: Palpitaciones, irritabilidad e insomnio diez semanas después de un parto sin complicaciones.
chief_complaint_i18n.nl: Palpitaties, prikkelbaarheid en slapeloosheid tien weken na een ongecompliceerde bevalling.
chief_complaint_i18n.ru: Сердцебиение, раздражительность и бессонница через десять недель после неосложнённых родов.

presentation.history_of_present_illness: Her first pregnancy was uncomplicated and she is breastfeeding. Symptoms began at about eight weeks postpartum and were initially attributed by her health visitor to sleep deprivation and possible postnatal depression. She has lost 3 kg beyond the expected postpartum loss, feels persistently hot, and describes a tremor when holding the baby. There is no neck pain and no eye symptom. She was screened at booking because of a family history of thyroid disease and was TPO antibody positive at 210 IU/mL with normal thyroid function - a detail that makes this presentation predictable rather than surprising.
past_medical_history: TPO antibody positive at antenatal booking with normal thyroid function
family_history: Sister: postpartum thyroiditis after both pregnancies
presentation.social_history: Non-smoker, no alcohol while breastfeeding. Supportive partner at home.

review_of_systems.general: Heat intolerance, 3 kg weight loss, fatigue disproportionate to the newborn
review_of_systems.psychiatric: Irritability and anxiety; Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale 9 - borderline, and confounded by the thyrotoxicosis

examination_findings: Small, firm, non-tender diffuse goitre (approximately 20 g)
No orbitopathy - no lid retraction, no proptosis, no chemosis
Fine tremor of the outstretched hands

results.interference_note: Note the modest FT3 rise relative to FT4. Destructive release leaks stored hormone in the gland's native T4-rich proportion, unlike Graves disease which preferentially secretes T3.
Raised from follicular destruction - excludes exogenous hormone and supports a destructive process.

lab_panels.comment: TRAb is the decisive request in a postpartum woman with thyrotoxicosis.

results.interference_note: Risen from the booking titre of 210 IU/mL - the postpartum rebound of immune tolerance that drives this condition.
Negative. This is what separates postpartum thyroiditis from postpartum Graves disease, which also peaks at 3-6 months and requires the opposite treatment.

lab_panels.comment: Week 18 postpartum. Symptoms resolving; no antithyroid drug was ever given.
Week 26 postpartum. Now symptomatically hypothyroid: cold, constipated, profoundly fatigued.
Week 38 postpartum, on levothyroxine 50 µg daily started at week 26 for symptomatic hypothyroidism.

lab_panels.panel_name: Thyroid function tests - after withdrawal trial
lab_panels.comment: Twelve months postpartum, six weeks after levothyroxine was withdrawn as a planned trial.

results.interference_note: In the upper half of the reference interval off treatment: euthyroid, but with a diminished reserve that carries a substantial lifetime risk of permanent hypothyroidism.

imaging.findings: Mildly enlarged gland (19 mL), diffusely hypoechoic and heterogeneous with normal-to-reduced vascularity. No nodule.
imaging.impression: Destructive pattern. Reduced vascularity distinguishes this from Graves disease. Radionuclide scanning was deliberately avoided because she is breastfeeding; the ultrasound plus a negative TRAb answered the question without interrupting feeding.

protocols.name: Phase-specific management of postpartum thyroiditis

name_i18n.es: Manejo por fases de la tiroiditis posparto

protocols.guideline_source: ATA 2017 guidelines for thyroid disease in pregnancy and the postpartum (adapted)
protocols.indication: Biphasic destructive thyroiditis in a TPO antibody positive woman at 10 weeks postpartum.

regimen.notes: Symptom control only. Compatible with breastfeeding at this dose; propranolol has low milk transfer.
The gland is leaking stored hormone, not synthesising it. Carbimazole would deepen and prolong the hypothyroid phase and add an agranulocytosis risk in a new mother.
Started for symptomatic hypothyroidism. Fully compatible with breastfeeding.
Because most cases recover, replacement must be presented as a trial from the outset and formally reviewed - not defaulted into lifelong treatment.

monitoring: TSH and FT4 every 4-8 weeks through the biphasic course
Recheck 6 weeks after any levothyroxine withdrawal trial
Annual TSH for life: roughly 20-30% develop permanent hypothyroidism
Counsel on a 70% recurrence risk in future pregnancies and check TSH at 6-12 weeks postpartum next time
Do not perform radionuclide uptake scanning while breastfeeding unless feeding is interrupted; ultrasound and TRAb usually suffice
contraindications: Thionamides are not indicated in the thyrotoxic phase of a destructive thyroiditis
adverse_effects: Iatrogenic hypothyroidism if a thionamide is given during the thyrotoxic phase
Unnecessary lifelong levothyroxine if the hypothyroid phase is treated without a withdrawal trial
protocols.notes: Postnatal depression and the hypothyroid phase overlap symptomatically and can coexist. Thyroid function should be checked before attributing postpartum mood change to depression alone - and a normal TSH does not exclude depression either.

diagnoses.label: Postpartum thyroiditis, classic triphasic course

label_i18n.es: Tiroiditis posparto de curso trifásico clásico
label_i18n.nl: Postpartum thyreoïditis met klassiek trifasisch beloop
label_i18n.ru: Послеродовой тиреоидит с классическим трёхфазным течением

diagnoses.discriminator: A negative TRAb with a raised thyroglobulin, reduced vascularity and spontaneous transition into a hypothyroid phase without any antithyroid treatment.
supporting_evidence: Onset at 10 weeks postpartum in a TPO antibody positive woman
TPO antibody rise from 210 to 486 IU/mL
TRAb negative at 0.7 IU/L
Thyroglobulin 142 µg/L - destructive release
Reduced vascularity on Doppler
Spontaneous resolution of thyrotoxicosis by week 18 with no thionamide
Hypothyroid phase at week 26 and euthyroidism off treatment at 12 months

diagnoses.label: Postpartum onset Graves disease

label_i18n.es: Enfermedad de Graves de inicio posparto

diagnoses.discriminator: The single most important alternative, since it peaks in the same postpartum window and requires a thionamide rather than watchful waiting. Excluded by a negative TRAb, reduced vascularity, absent orbitopathy and spontaneous resolution.
supporting_evidence: Thyrotoxicosis in the postpartum window
Diffuse goitre

diagnoses.label: Postnatal depression
diagnoses.discriminator: Not mutually exclusive. The EPDS of 9 is borderline and confounded by thyrotoxicosis; it must be reassessed once euthyroid rather than dismissed or acted on now.
supporting_evidence: Irritability, insomnia, fatigue, EPDS 9
refuting_evidence: Symptoms tracked the biochemistry through both phases
Objective signs of thyrotoxicosis: tachycardia, tremor, goitre

teaching_points: Postpartum thyroiditis is biphasic. Treating the thyrotoxic phase with a thionamide is not merely useless - it deepens and prolongs the hypothyroid phase that follows.
TRAb is the decisive test in postpartum thyrotoxicosis. Postpartum Graves disease presents in the same window and requires the opposite management.

Levothyroxine started for the hypothyroid phase must be framed as a trial with a planned withdrawal at around 12 months, or the patient is silently converted to a lifelong prescription she does not need.

TPO antibody status at booking is genuinely predictive: roughly 30-50% of antibody-positive women develop postpartum thyroiditis, and a documented booking titre transforms the interpretation of a postpartum presentation.
Radionuclide scanning is avoidable here. Ultrasound with Doppler plus TRAb answers the question without interrupting breastfeeding.
About 20-30% of women develop permanent hypothyroidism, and recurrence in a subsequent pregnancy approaches 70%. Both figures belong in the discharge letter.

references.citation: Alexander EK et al. 2017 ATA Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Thyroid Disease During Pregnancy and the Postpartum. Thyroid.

must_include_findings.label: Spontaneous transition to a hypothyroid phase

expected_management: counsel on recurrence in future pregnancy

safety_rules.description: Must not recommend carbimazole or propylthiouracil for the thyrotoxic phase.
Levothyroxine, if started, should be accompanied by a planned withdrawal trial.
Should account for breastfeeding when proposing radionuclide imaging.

cases.summary: The discordant pattern with a genuinely short differential: assay interference, resistance to thyroid hormone, or a TSH-secreting adenoma. This case works through all three and lands on resistance, confirmed by THRB sequencing and by an affected father.

summary_i18n.en: Discordant TFTs worked through interference, resistance to thyroid hormone and TSH-secreting adenoma; THRB sequencing settles it.
summary_i18n.de: Diskordante Schilddrüsenwerte: Abklärung von Interferenz, Schilddrüsenhormonresistenz und TSH-produzierendem Adenom; THRB-Sequenzierung entscheidet.
summary_i18n.es: Pruebas tiroideas discordantes evaluadas para interferencia, resistencia a hormonas tiroideas y adenoma secretor de TSH; la secuenciación de THRB lo resuelve.
summary_i18n.nl: Discordante schildklierwaarden: interferentie, schildklierhormoonresistentie en TSH-producerend adenoom afgewogen; THRB-sequencing geeft de doorslag.
summary_i18n.ru: Дискордантные тиреоидные показатели: рассмотрены интерференция, резистентность к тиреоидным гормонам и ТТГ-секретирующая аденома; вопрос решает секвенирование THRB.

cases.author: MedSimQA Editorial

presentation.chief_complaint: Referred after an incidental abnormal thyroid profile found during investigation of a resting tachycardia; a previous clinician had started carbimazole, which made him hypothyroid without normalising the TSH.

chief_complaint_i18n.en: Incidental abnormal thyroid profile; carbimazole started previously made him hypothyroid without normalising TSH.
chief_complaint_i18n.de: Zufällig auffälliges Schilddrüsenprofil; zuvor begonnenes Carbimazol führte zur Hypothyreose ohne TSH-Normalisierung.
chief_complaint_i18n.es: Perfil tiroideo anómalo incidental; el carbimazol iniciado previamente le provocó hipotiroidismo sin normalizar la TSH.
chief_complaint_i18n.nl: Toevallig afwijkend schildklierprofiel; eerder gestart carbimazol maakte hem hypothyreoot zonder TSH-normalisatie.
chief_complaint_i18n.ru: Случайно выявленный патологический тиреоидный профиль; ранее назначенный карбимазол вызвал гипотиреоз, но ТТГ не нормализовался.

presentation.history_of_present_illness: He has always had a resting heart rate around 95-100 bpm and a mild tremor, which he regards as normal for him. He is not heat intolerant, his weight is stable, and he performs well academically. A previous clinician interpreted the raised free T4 as thyrotoxicosis, started carbimazole 20 mg, and stopped it after eight weeks when the patient became fatigued and constipated while the TSH ROSE rather than fell. His father has 'unusual thyroid tests' that have been investigated three times at different hospitals without a diagnosis, and a paternal aunt was treated for hyperthyroidism with radioiodine and is now on levothyroxine.
past_medical_history: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder diagnosed in childhood
Recurrent otitis media as a child with mild high-frequency hearing loss
Delayed bone age noted at age 12

medications.name: Carbimazole
medications.notes: Caused symptomatic hypothyroidism with a rising TSH - a pharmacological experiment that, read correctly, already pointed to the diagnosis.

family_history: Father: long-standing unexplained abnormal thyroid function tests, never diagnosed
Paternal aunt: treated with radioiodine for 'hyperthyroidism', now hypothyroid
Pattern consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
presentation.social_history: Non-smoker, occasional alcohol, no supplements and specifically no biotin.

review_of_systems.cardiovascular: Long-standing resting tachycardia, palpitations on exertion only
review_of_systems.general: Stable weight, no heat intolerance, no night sweats
review_of_systems.neurological: Mild tremor since adolescence, childhood ADHD

examination_findings: Small diffuse goitre (approximately 25 g), soft and non-tender
Visual fields full to confrontation - relevant to excluding a pituitary macroadenoma
No features of McCune-Albright syndrome, normal secondary sexual characteristics

lab_panels.comment: Four weeks after stopping carbimazole. The defining discordant pattern.

results.interference_note: A NORMAL TSH is the abnormality. With an FT4 of 32.4 pmol/L, a normally functioning pituitary would have suppressed TSH to below 0.05. An 'inappropriately normal' TSH is a positive finding, not a reassuring one.
Total and free hormone move together, arguing against a binding-protein abnormality such as familial dysalbuminaemic hyperthyroxinaemia.

lab_panels.comment: The three questions in order: is it real, is it a tumour, is it resistance?

results.value_text: TSH 3.6 mIU/L, FT4 31.8 pmol/L - concordant with the primary platform
results.interference_note: Interference excluded first, because it is the commonest cause of a discordant pattern and the cheapest to rule out.
A ratio above 1.0 suggests a TSH-secreting adenoma. At 0.4 this argues strongly against a TSHoma.

Decisive. SHBG is a hepatic marker of thyroid hormone ACTION. In a TSH-secreting adenoma the liver is genuinely thyrotoxic and SHBG is high; in resistance the mutant receptor blunts hepatic response and SHBG stays normal. A normal SHBG with an FT4 of 32.4 means the tissues are not thyrotoxic.

lab_panels.panel_name: TRH stimulation and T3 suppression testing
lab_panels.comment: Dynamic testing to separate resistance from a TSH-secreting adenoma.

results.analyte_name: Peak TSH after TRH 200 µg IV
results.interference_note: A preserved, brisk TSH response to TRH. Autonomous adenomas classically show a blunted or absent response, so this argues for resistance.

results.analyte_name: TSH after 8 days of liothyronine 100 µg/day
results.ref_text: Partial suppression expected in resistance; none in TSHoma
results.interference_note: Partial suppression from 3.8 to 0.9 mIU/L. The axis is regulatable but at a reset, higher set-point - the physiological signature of resistance. A TSHoma would have suppressed minimally or not at all.

lab_panels.comment: THRB sequencing on the proband and his father.

results.value_text: Heterozygous missense variant NM_000461.5:c.1012C>T p.(Arg338Trp), classified pathogenic (ACMG class 5)
results.interference_note: Located in the T3-binding domain hotspot. Acts by dominant negative inhibition: the mutant receptor still binds DNA and RXR but cannot bind T3, and it blocks the wild-type allele.

results.value_text: Same heterozygous variant p.(Arg338Trp) detected; father's FT4 29.8 pmol/L with TSH 4.2 mIU/L
results.interference_note: Family segregation confirms pathogenicity and, incidentally, explains three previous inconclusive workups in the father.

lab_panels.panel_name: Peripheral markers of thyroid hormone action
lab_panels.comment: Additional evidence that the tissues are not thyrotoxic despite the high free hormones.

results.interference_note: True thyrotoxicosis lowers cholesterol; a mid-range value here indicates a normal hepatic thyroid state.
No high bone turnover - again unlike true thyrotoxicosis.

imaging.findings: Normal pituitary gland, 5 mm in height, homogeneous enhancement. No microadenoma or macroadenoma. Stalk midline, chiasm normal.
imaging.impression: Normal. Together with an alpha-subunit:TSH ratio of 0.4 and a preserved TRH response, this effectively excludes a TSH-secreting adenoma.

imaging.findings: Normal chamber dimensions, LVEF 62%, no left ventricular hypertrophy, normal diastolic function.
imaging.impression: No structural consequence of the resting tachycardia. Supports a cardiac phenotype driven by relatively unopposed TR-alpha signalling rather than by systemic thyrotoxicosis.

protocols.name: Observation with selective beta-blockade for resistance to thyroid hormone beta

name_i18n.en: Observation with selective beta-blockade for resistance to thyroid hormone beta
name_i18n.de: Beobachtung mit selektiver Betablockade bei Schilddrüsenhormonresistenz (RTH-beta)
name_i18n.es: Observación con betabloqueo selectivo en la resistencia a hormonas tiroideas beta
name_i18n.nl: Observatie met selectieve bètablokkade bij schildklierhormoonresistentie bèta
name_i18n.ru: Наблюдение с селективной бета-блокадой при резистентности к тиреоидным гормонам бета

protocols.guideline_source: Composite of published RTH-beta cohort management practice
protocols.indication: Genetically confirmed dominant negative THRB variant with compensated peripheral euthyroidism and an isolated cardiac phenotype.

regimen.notes: The raised free hormones are compensatory and necessary to achieve normal signalling through the mutant receptor. Lowering them produces tissue hypothyroidism, exactly as happened on carbimazole.
Beta-1 selective. The cardiac phenotype is mediated largely through TR-alpha, which is not mutated, so the heart genuinely does see excess hormone even while the liver and pituitary do not.
First-degree relatives should be offered THRB testing. It prevents exactly the inappropriate ablation that occurred in the paternal aunt.
A prominent record entry stating that the abnormal thyroid results are expected and must not be treated. Without it, the next clinician repeats the carbimazole error.

monitoring: Annual review of heart rate, weight, growth in affected children, and symptoms
Do NOT titrate free T4 towards the reference interval - it is the wrong target in this condition

Pre-conception counselling: a euthyroid fetus carrying the wild-type allele is exposed to the mother's high free T4 and is at risk of miscarriage and low birth weight, so an affected mother may need dose-adjusted management in pregnancy
Audiology and developmental follow-up in affected children, given the association with hearing loss and ADHD
contraindications: Thionamides, radioiodine and thyroidectomy are all contraindicated and are the principal iatrogenic hazard of this condition
adverse_effects: Iatrogenic hypothyroidism from any attempt to normalise the free T4
protocols.notes: The paternal aunt in this family was treated with radioiodine for presumed hyperthyroidism and now requires levothyroxine at supraphysiological doses - the natural history of a missed diagnosis, and the reason cascade testing matters.

diagnoses.label: Resistance to thyroid hormone beta (THRB p.Arg338Trp)

label_i18n.en: Resistance to thyroid hormone beta (THRB p.Arg338Trp)
label_i18n.es: Resistencia a hormonas tiroideas beta (THRB p.Arg338Trp)
label_i18n.ru: Резистентность к тиреоидным гормонам бета (THRB p.Arg338Trp)

diagnoses.discriminator: Pathogenic THRB variant segregating with the phenotype in an affected father, plus a normal SHBG, a normal alpha-subunit:TSH ratio, a preserved TRH response, partial T3 suppressibility and a normal pituitary MRI.
supporting_evidence: FT4 32.4 and FT3 9.4 pmol/L with a non-suppressed TSH of 3.8 mIU/L
Concordant results on a second, non-biotin platform - interference excluded
SHBG 34 nmol/L (normal) despite high free hormones - tissues are not thyrotoxic
Alpha-subunit:TSH molar ratio 0.4
Preserved TSH response to TRH and partial suppression on liothyronine
Normal pituitary MRI
Heterozygous pathogenic THRB p.(Arg338Trp) in proband and affected father
Iatrogenic hypothyroidism on carbimazole with a paradoxically rising TSH

diagnoses.label: TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma (TSHoma)
diagnoses.discriminator: The critical alternative, because it is a treatable tumour. Excluded by a normal alpha-subunit:TSH ratio, a normal SHBG, a preserved TRH response, partial T3 suppressibility, a normal MRI, and a positive family history with a segregating variant.
supporting_evidence: Non-suppressed TSH with raised free hormones is common to both
refuting_evidence: SHBG normal - in a TSHoma the liver is thyrotoxic and SHBG is raised
Autosomal dominant family history with a confirmed THRB variant

diagnoses.label: Assay interference (biotin, heterophile antibody, anti-T4 antibody)
diagnoses.discriminator: Always the first thing to exclude in a discordant pattern, because it is the commonest cause and the cheapest to rule out. Here, results were concordant across two platforms and serum biotin was normal.
refuting_evidence: Concordant results on a non-biotin platform
Total and free hormones move together

diagnoses.label: Familial dysalbuminaemic hyperthyroxinaemia
diagnoses.discriminator: Also autosomal dominant with a raised T4 and normal TSH, but free T3 is normal and the abnormality is assay-dependent, disappearing on equilibrium dialysis. Here FT3 is genuinely raised.
supporting_evidence: Autosomal dominant family history
Raised total and free T4

teaching_points: An 'inappropriately normal' TSH alongside raised free hormones is a positive finding. The differential is short: assay interference, resistance to thyroid hormone, or a TSH-secreting adenoma.
Exclude interference first. It is the commonest explanation and needs only a second platform and a serum biotin.

SHBG is the most informative single discriminator between resistance and a TSHoma. It reports hepatic thyroid hormone ACTION: normal in resistance, raised in a TSHoma, where the liver really is thyrotoxic.
An alpha-subunit:TSH molar ratio above 1.0 points to a TSHoma; a preserved TRH response and partial T3 suppressibility point to resistance.

The tissue-specific phenotype follows receptor distribution. TR-beta predominates in the pituitary and liver and is mutated, so those tissues are resistant; TR-alpha predominates in the heart and is normal, so tachycardia coexists with a normal SHBG and normal cholesterol.
A trial of carbimazole in this condition causes iatrogenic hypothyroidism with a paradoxically rising TSH. Read correctly, that failed trial is itself diagnostic information.
Cascade testing prevents real harm. The paternal aunt in this family was ablated with radioiodine for a disease she never had.
Never titrate the free T4 into the reference interval in resistance to thyroid hormone. The elevated free hormone is the compensation, not the disease.

references.citation: Refetoff S, Dumitrescu AM. Syndromes of reduced sensitivity to thyroid hormone. Best Pract Res Clin Endocrinol Metab 2007.
Beck-Peccoz P et al. 2013 ETA Guidelines: The Diagnosis and Management of Central Hypothyroidism and TSH-secreting adenomas. Eur Thyroid J.

must_include_findings.label: Non-suppressed TSH with raised free hormones
Normal SHBG indicating absent peripheral thyrotoxicosis

expected_management: document to prevent future inappropriate treatment

safety_rules.description: Must not recommend antithyroid drugs, radioiodine or thyroidectomy.
Must explicitly consider and exclude a TSH-secreting adenoma before settling on resistance.
